messages:
samir: Heads-up — EdgeWave wants a Dedicated commit for EU-edge starting Jul 1. They asked for sustained 300 GPU-hours/day (p4d-eq) with 25% burstable headroom and multi-region failover to US-west. Need quick sizing + tradeoffs for pricing and network constraints.

ellie: 300 GPU-hrs/day sustained -> ~9k GPU-hrs/month. With 25% headroom that's 11.25k GPU-hrs/month. Do we want to price pure reserved for the full headroom or reserved + burst credits? :thinking:

kevin: Quick calc:
```
Sustained = 300 hr/day
Monthly ~= 300 * 30 = 9000 hr
Headroom = 9000 * 0.25 = 2250 hr
Commit = 9000 + 2250 = 11250 hr/month
```
If our p4d-eq cost baseline is X/hr, that's straightforward. But network egress and cross-region replication add non-trivial cost and latency.

maya: On network: EU->US failover will double some egress on warm standby if they want hot replicas. We could offer cold standby (snapshot restore ~30–90m) to save money. Also we need to check pod density on eu-central-1 GPUs in July; calendar shows pre-booked capacity for infra experiments.

samir: Good point. Two options to present:
- Option A: Reserved commit = full 11.25k hr/month priced at a discount, includes soft 25% burst allowance (we throttle non-critical jobs to stay under). No guaranteed cross-region hot standby.
- Option B: Reserved for sustained (9k hr) + burst credits bucket of 2.25k hr month at premium; add optional hot-replica pool in US-west billed as separate reserved or on-demand.
Which is operationally easier?

ellie: Option B is better for us ops-wise — avoids overcommitting eu GPUs and gives explicit billing for hot failover. We should surface estimated restore times and SLO impacts.

kevin: Also runbook impact: Option A requires autoscaling policies and stricter request shaping to prevent noisy neighbors. Option B needs token-bucket accounting for burst credits + a small reserved pool in secondary region if they want <1min failover.

samir: EdgeWave is sensitive to latency for LiveChat. They said <150ms p50 EU only; US failover acceptable at p50 <300ms. So hot replicas in EU only, US for DR. We should design pricing accordingly.

maya: Capacity note: our capacity forecast for eu-central shows a 12% utilization bump in July due to R&D experiments. If we sell them full 25% headroom, ops risk higher spike days. Can we propose a dynamic headroom that scales by weekday/weekend and seasonal windows?

kevin: We can offer a two-tier headroom: base 15% always reserved, additional 10% burst credits that expire monthly. Works well with our batch cache and prefix caching to reduce steady-state tokens.

samir: Draft pricing language to send to sales: include formula and examples. Also include a fingerprint of worst-case cost: commit * hr_rate + eg + cross-region replica cost.

ellie: I'll draft the formula. Example block to include: 
```
Example (p4d-eq rate = $10/hr):
Sustained: 300 * 24 * 30 * $10 ~= $72,000
Headroom(25%): +$18,000 -> Commit $90,000/month
Burst credits (Option B): 2250 hr * $12 (premium) = $27,000
Hot-replica US-west reserved (optional): 2000 hr * $8 = $16,000
```

maya: Ops ask: If they want hot-replica in EU+US simultaneously, we need cross-region KV sync and higher egress. Add note: multi-region hot replicate adds ~15-20% additional infra cost and 10-30ms added tail latency.

ops-bot: quota_request_submitted: EdgeWave-Dedicated-eu-central-11250hrs (ticket #4629).

samir: Thanks — @ellie can you put a short pros/cons and the two pricing examples into a one-pager for Sales? I'll loop in account exec after that. Also confirm eu-central node availability windows for July 1.

ellie: On it. Will ping infra-capacity with timeline and cc @kevin for the runbook bits. ETA EOD today. :thumbsup:

kevin: If infra-capacity flags risk, propose staggered rollout (start with 15% headroom, then scale to 25% after 30 days). That reduces risk and gives time to tune autoscaler.

samir: Perfect. Let's proceed with Option B as primary + staged headroom ramp. I'll keep Sales in the loop.
